family.description: This is the serine protease domain of MIP (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin protease), a protein that is related to pathogenicity of animal and human pathogenic Mycoplasmas [[cite:PUB00098027],[cite:PUB00098028],[cite:PUB00098029],[cite:PUB00151017]]. This protein functions together with the Ig binding protein M (MIB) to evade host Ig-mediated defense against the MIB-MIP system, which is a novel mechanism that protects mycoplasma against host immune response [[cite:PUB00098028],[cite:PUB00151017]]. MIB tightly interacts to the antigen-binding fragment (Fab) and recruits the MIP protease that is activated and cleaves the IgG heavy chain, disrupting the antigen binding site. Therefore, the MIB-MIP system appears to be crucial to mycoplasma immune evasion [[cite:PUB00151017]].
family.name: Mycoplasma immunoglobulin protease

evidence.explanation: Figure 2C joint WT lane and immunoblot controls, visually inspected; Figure 2B provides corroborating pulled-down serum substrate.

evidence.explanation: Figure 2C r-0582A lane, Results and Figure S5; residue-numbering discrepancy explicitly retained.

edges.subject: published-r0582a

evidence.explanation: Figure 3B Fab immunoblot lanes and caption, visually inspected.

edges.mechanism: The joint preparation cleaves the Fab substrate, producing the displayed antibody-reactive fragment; no exact cleavage bond or rate is assigned.
edges.subject: joint-fab

evidence.explanation: Figure 3B F(ab')2 lanes and caption; Figure 3C Edman result retained as context, not a universal residue coordinate.

edges.subject: joint-fab2

causal_graphs.family_mapping: MIP82/MMCAP2_0582 reference ACU78687.1 (861 aa) exactly matches UniParc UPI0001793D5F, PF01732 290-776. MIB83/MMCAP2_0583 is ACU78312.1 (750 aa), a distinct binding protein. Historical recombinant termini and the r-0582A clone sequence are not independently verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: DIRECT refers to net purified-preparation effects, not an isolated PF01732 domain or an atomic catalytic step. The paper's S727A label conflicts with Y727/S759 in the full-length reference and S759A in 2021; retain r-0582A without asserting a canonical residue. Folding effects are not excluded. VH/CH numbering and exact cleavage-bond identity remain unresolved; no universal substrate or inhibitor rule.

causal_graphs.context: Cleavage assays use about 1e9 washed late-exponential cells in 15 ul SP5 without FBS, 100 ng/ul purified serum IgG or 2% albumin-depleted D12 goat serum, 30 min at 37 C, supernatant immunoblot. Agglutination is a different overnight static 37 C assay; Methods give 4% serum and caption 2%. D0 serum does not produce the same cellular IgM cleavage/agglutination response.

evidence.explanation: Figure 5F micrographs and OD310 panel, with D0 and single-pair comparators; 2%/4% serum discrepancy retained.

edges.mechanism: Under the distinct overnight D12-serum protocol the deleted strain forms visible aggregates and higher settled-aggregate OD310 than WT.
edges.subject: whole-locus-deletion

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The deleted cluster includes MIP82/MMCAP2_0582, ACU78687.1 with PF01732 290-776, but also three other MIPs and four MIBs. Whole-locus effects cannot be attributed exclusively to this protein or its domain. Main Figure 5B establishes the design; exact strain lineage and nucleotide breakpoints in inaccessible supplements remain unverified here.
causal_graphs.limitations: INDIRECT genotype effects. Single-pair retention is not reintroduction complementation. Anti-HRP IgG is not detectably cleaved by cells despite purified-system activity. OD310 measures settled aggregates, not growth. Results panel cross-references are offset; actual Figure 5C/E/F is used. Low-resolution visual inspection supports qualitative direction, not numeric effect sizes or a domain-specific mechanism.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: MIP82/MMCAP2_0582 is the PF01732-bearing ACU78687.1 reference, residues 290-776; all four MIB/MIP pairs remain in these ATPase mutants. ATPase beta-like 0575 is a partner, not the PF01732 protein. K152A belongs to 0575 and occurs with G3S/K4R, not as an isolated substitution against WT.
causal_graphs.limitations: INDIRECT cellular effects with one clone per genotype, other SNPs/INDELs, no complementation and extra DeltaATPase passages/23S-rRNA changes. MIB/MIP abundances are broadly WT-like but localization/assembly are unresolved. No ATP-hydrolysis rate, transmembrane energy transfer or release/reset transition was measured. The proposed model predicts pellet cleavage products not clearly observed. May 2026 correction concerns acknowledgements, not experimental data.

record.description: This is the serine protease domain of MIP (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin protease), a protein that is related to pathogenicity of animal and human pathogenic Mycoplasmas [[cite:PUB00098027],[cite:PUB00098028],[cite:PUB00098029],[cite:PUB00151017]]. This protein functions together with the Ig binding protein M (MIB) to evade host Ig-mediated defense against the MIB-MIP system, which is a novel mechanism that protects mycoplasma against host immune response [[cite:PUB00098028],[cite:PUB00151017]]. MIB tightly interacts to the antigen-binding fragment (Fab) and recruits the MIP protease that is activated and cleaves the IgG heavy chain, disrupting the antigen binding site. Therefore, the MIB-MIP system appears to be crucial to mycoplasma immune evasion [[cite:PUB00151017]].

evidence.explanation: Joint cleavage, MIB omission and published r-0582A effects are supported; clone numbering and exact antibody cleavage bond remain unresolved.
Active and inactive joint mixtures dissociate antigen complexes, and MIB alone also acts. Cleavage is not required for this endpoint.

discussions.notes: Preserve frozen source bytes but do not repeat its conflation of MIB with Protein M. The exact ACU78687.1/UPI0001793D5F sequence maps PF01732 290-776. Retired A0A446C0V0 has a different whole-protein reference at residue 810; do not use it as an exact GM12 mapping. Reconcile CH numbering and antibody sequences before assigning a cleavage bond.
discussions.prompt: Resolve historical construct numbering and distinguish MIP, MIB and Protein M.
discussions.rationale: The exact GM12 MIP reference supports PF01732 membership but not isolated-domain sufficiency. The 2016 S727A label conflicts with full-length Y727/S759 and the 2021 S759A label; historical plasmid sequencing is needed before canonical residue-level claims.

evidence.explanation: Whole-locus deletion affects cleavage and D12-serum agglutination; retained single-pair cells are not a reintroduction rescue. Supplements and exact strain breakpoints remain unassessed.
ATPase deletion and recode-matched K152A-associated effects support system dependence but not measured ATP hydrolysis or the proposed opening/reset mechanism.
